# @nospt/backstage-plugin-apigee

The **frontend** package of the [Backstage Apigee plugin](../../README.md) — a dedicated **API Hub** experience for browsing the Apigee proxies and Apigee API Hub definitions that the [backend module](../apigee-backend/README.md) syncs into your catalog.

Built on the Backstage **New Frontend System**.

## What you get

- **API Hub dashboard** (`/api-hub`) — an overview with live counts of your APIs by lifecycle (production / experimental / deprecated) and quick links into the catalog.
- **API catalog** (`/api-hub/catalog`) — a searchable, paginated grid of API cards with:
  - facet filters for **lifecycle**, **org**, **owner**, and **department**;
  - full-text search and a configurable page-size selector;
  - a details drawer showing metadata and the embedded or linked OpenAPI/AsyncAPI spec.
- **Shareable views** — filters, search, and paging are all reflected in the URL (`?lifecycle=`, `?org=`, `?owner=`, `?department=`, `?q=`, `?page=`, `?size=`), so any view can be bookmarked or shared.

The catalog only shows entities produced by the Apigee backend (identified by their `cloud.google.com/*` annotations), so it lives happily alongside the rest of your Backstage catalog.

## Routes

| Path               | Tab         | Description                                       |
| ------------------ | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `/api-hub`         | Home        | Landing dashboard with API stats and quick links. |
| `/api-hub/catalog` | API catalog | Filterable, searchable grid of API entities.      |

## Installation

Add the package to your app:

```bash
yarn --cwd packages/app add @nospt/backstage-plugin-apigee
```

Register the plugin in `packages/app/src/App.tsx`:

```ts
import apigeePlugin from '@nospt/backstage-plugin-apigee';

export const app = createApp({
  features: [
    // ...
    apigeePlugin,
  ],
});
```

### Optional: grouped navigation

The package also exports `apigeeNavModule`, a New Frontend System nav module that renders an expandable **API Hub** group (with the Home and API catalog sub-pages) in the app sidebar. Add it to your app's features to enable it:

```ts
import apigeePlugin, { apigeeNavModule } from '@nospt/backstage-plugin-apigee';

export const app = createApp({
  features: [apigeePlugin, apigeeNavModule],
});
```

If you manage the sidebar with your own nav module, skip `apigeeNavModule` and link to `/api-hub` directly.

## Configuration

All frontend settings are optional and live under `apigee.catalog`:

```yaml
apigee:
  catalog:
    # Friendly labels for the "Org" filter facet: raw org id -> display label.
    orgLabels:
      apigee-x-private-p-495866: Private
      apigee-x-public-p-863498: Public
    # Initial API cards per page. Users can change it via the selector
    # (10/20/30/40/50). Values below 1 are floored to 1; defaults to 10.
    pageSize: 24
```

| Key                        | Type   | Default | Description                                                                                                  |
| -------------------------- | ------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `apigee.catalog.orgLabels` | map    | —       | Maps raw org ids to friendly labels shown in the **Org** facet. Unmapped ids fall back to a humanised label. |
| `apigee.catalog.pageSize`  | number | `10`    | Initial page size for the catalog grid.                                                                      |

The entities themselves (and everything shown on the cards) come from the backend module — see its [configuration reference](../apigee-backend/README.md#configuration).

## Development

```bash
cd plugins/apigee
yarn start    # run the isolated dev harness
yarn test     # unit tests
yarn test:e2e # Playwright end-to-end tests
yarn lint
yarn build
```
